# General

```{r}
library(glmmTMB)
library(dplyr)
library(DHARMa)
library(emmeans)
library(car)
```

```{r, echo=F}
env <- read.table("/home/danielred/data/work/projects/eDNA_filters/environment.tsv", header=T)
data <- read.table("/home/danielred/data/work/projects/eDNA_filters/data.tsv", header=T)
```
The manuscript lacks an appropriate statistical framework for the field data. The most important weakness is the treatment of field detections as independent observations. The design is inherently hierarchical (8 localities, sampled 3 times, 5 sites pooled per locality, 3 filter types, 3 replicate filters, 3 technical amplification replicates), yet most results are summarized as counts, positivity rates, or scores. **A more appropriate analysis would involve a generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) framework, possibly using locality as a random effect, sampling event as a repeated factor, filter type as fixed effect, assay type as fixed effect, turbidity as covariate.**

At present it is difficult to determine whether apparent differences among filter types or assays remain significant after accounting for repeated sampling and non-independence. The current use of ANOVA appears restricted primarily to laboratory experiments and filtered volume comparisons.

# data 

```{r}
str(data)
sum(is.na(data$presence))
with(data, table(amplificance_method, is.na(presence)))

data <- data |>
  mutate(across(c(location, season, filter, amplificance_method, samplingId), factor),
         volume   = as.numeric( trimws(volume, whitespace = "[ \\h\\v]") ), # trim unicode ws too
         presence = as.integer(presence))



snail <- data |>
  filter(amplificance_method == "snail") |>
  group_by(samplingId) |>
  summarise(snail = as.integer(any(presence == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
            consistent = n_distinct(na.omit(presence)) <= 1, .groups = "drop")

all(snail$consistent)

edna <- data |>
  filter(amplificance_method != "snail", !is.na(presence)) |>
  droplevels() |>
  left_join(snail, by = "samplingId") |>
  mutate(sampleId = interaction(samplingId, filter, replication, drop = TRUE),
         turb_z   = as.numeric(scale(log(turbidity))),
         amplificance_method = relevel(amplificance_method, "qPCR"))

edna_agg <- edna |>
  group_by(location, season, samplingId, sampleId, filter, amplificance_method, turb_z, snail) |>
  summarise(pos = sum(presence), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

# stat 1

- `season` should be random effect?
- `sampleId` is made from `samplingID` (`location` + `date`) + `filter` + `replication` $\to$ should I discard some re?
- maybe easiest is to make a full model and then do model selection on it (exclude turbulence, etc)

```{r}
m1 <- glmmTMB(presence ~ filter * amplificance_method + turb_z + season +
                (1 | location) + (1 | samplingId) + (1 | sampleId),
              family = binomial, data = edna)

m2 <- update(m1, . ~ . + filter:turb_z)      # does turbidity affect filters differently?
anova(m1, m2)
```

m1 AIC is smaller, btw anova non-sign $\to$ proceed with m1

```{r}
summary(m1)
Anova(m1, type = "II")
```

filter type and amplification method is signif. Interesting is, that their interaction is also signif.

## diagnostics

```{r}
res <- simulateResiduals(m1)
plot(res)
testDispersion(res)
```

## Post-hoc

filters within each method, and methods within each filter

```{r}
emmeans(m1, pairwise ~ filter | amplificance_method, type = "response")
emmeans(m1, pairwise ~ amplificance_method | filter, type = "response")
```

so at qPCR filter type matters, with LAMP it does not

LAMP is similar as RAA, but they are different then qPCR

# stat 2

```{r}
m1_agg <- glmmTMB(cbind(pos, n - pos) ~ filter * amplificance_method + turb_z + season +
                    (1 | location) + (1 | samplingId) + (1 | sampleId),
                  family = binomial, data = edna_agg) # or family = betabinomial 

summary(m1_agg)
Anova(m1_agg, type = "II")
```

## diag

```{r}
res <- simulateResiduals(m1_agg)
plot(res)
testDispersion(res)
```

## post-hoc

```{r}
emmeans(m1_agg, pairwise ~ filter | amplificance_method, type = "response")
emmeans(m1_agg, pairwise ~ amplificance_method | filter, type = "response")
```

I would say use the non-aggregated model...

# stat 3

eDNA detection <- snail parasited?

```{r}
m_snail <- update(m1, . ~ . + snail)
summary(m_snail)
```

# stat 4

Detection sensitivity: only events where infected snails were found

```{r}
m_sens <- update(m1, data = subset(edna, snail == 1))
summary(m_sens)
```

## post-hoc 

```{r}
emmeans(m_sens, pairwise ~ filter | amplificance_method, type = "response")
```

# stat 5

Event-level agreement with snails (sensitivity / specificity per filter × method)

- sensitivity: percent when par detected (in cases when snails confirm par presence)
- specificity: percent when par not detected (when snails did not have parasites)

```{r}
edna |>
  group_by(samplingId, filter, amplificance_method, snail) |>
  summarise(edna_pos = as.integer(any(presence == 1)), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(filter, amplificance_method) |>
  summarise(sensitivity = mean(edna_pos[snail == 1]),
            specificity = 1 - mean(edna_pos[snail == 0]),
            n_snail_pos = sum(snail == 1), .groups = "drop")
```
